judge_verdict.summary: Agent correctly implemented PWM loading and KLD but its generate_dna diverges from the required construction, causing Step 76.4 scan_sequence integration tests to fail.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault partial failure—the verifier's FAIL is correct. The hidden harness found /app/solution.py and awarded binary_reward 0 with fractional score 0.667 after Steps 76.1 and 76.2 passed but Step 76.4 failed on an assertion that scan_sequence(sequence, load_motif_from_df(data), 0.8) must match a precomputed target [1][2]. The task required four integrated functions in /app/solution.py, including generate_dna that builds a uniform-length background, its reverse complement, and a PWM-sampled insertion at a random position p with 0 ≤ p < N, then scan_sequence that thresholds log-odds at scale·KLD and returns the most frequent hit over num_runs [3][4]. The agent implemented load_motif_from_df and compute_kld correctly (matching reference L2-normalize-after-+1 and Σ p·log(p/0.25)) [2][5], but its generate_dna first samples the N-length uniform background and PWM motif, only then draws p, and builds new_seq_rc by reverse-complementing the already-extended new_seq rather than reverse-complementing the N-length uniform background and inserting the spike at N−p [6][7]. Because Step 76.4 tests seed random to 42, call the agent's own generate_dna, and assert scan_sequence on that sequence against reference targets, this ordering and RC construction produce a different insertion index and sequence (e.g., p=148 vs the reference p=163 for the first test case) even though the agent's scan_sequence logic matches the reference when given the same input sequence [4][6][7]. The agent ran only ad-hoc self-tests on its own pipeline—reporting 13/20 and 109/200 recovery rates—and concluded the solution was correct without exercising the seeded generate_dna contract that the verifier indirectly enforces [8][9]. Steps 1–2 are sound, but the task as a whole is not solved, so TN is appropriate and the verifier is not at fault.

judge_verdict.summary: The agent implemented steps 76.1–76.2 correctly but its generate_dna and scan_sequence diverge from the task spec, so the verifier's Step 76.4 failure is justified.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a genuine agent-fault failure where the verifier's FAIL is correct. The hidden harness found `/app/solution.py`, passed Steps 76.1 and 76.2, skipped 76.3 as indirectly covered, and failed Step 76.4 on `assert np.allclose(scan_sequence(sequence, load_motif_from_df(data),0.8), target)` with fractional reward 2/3 and `binary_reward` 0 [1]. The task required four coupled functions in one file: L2-normalized PWM loading, uniform-background KLD, a DNA generator that inserts a PWM-sampled motif at a random index `< length` and returns the reverse complement, and a multi-run scanner that records every window start whose log-odds exceeds `scale * compute_kld(matrix)` then returns the most frequent position [2]. The reference solution samples insertion with `random.randint(0, N-1)`, draws motif nucleotides from raw PWM weights, builds the reverse complement separately before motif insertion, and appends every threshold-passing window start across all runs before taking the mode [3][4]. The agent instead constrained insertion to `random.randrange(0, N - motif_length + 1)`, sampled motif bases from renormalized L2-normalized PWM rows, derived the reverse complement by translating and reversing the full inserted sequence, and in `scan_sequence` kept only the highest-scoring window per run before counting modes [5][6]. Because Step 76.4 tests call the submitted `generate_dna` under `random.seed(42)` and compare `scan_sequence` output to HDF5 targets baked from the reference behavior, these semantic mismatches necessarily break the end-to-end binding-site detection check even though earlier steps passed [7][8]. The agent wrote the file into an empty `/app` workspace and declared success after only `py_compile` and a toy sanity check with `num_runs=5` on a hand-made PWM, which was too weak to exercise seeded integration cases [9]. The task was not truly solved, and the verifier's rejection is fair, so this is TN [1][5][6][8].

judge_verdict.summary: Agent delivered a partial solution with wrong log base in KLD/scanning and incorrect motif insertion in generate_dna; verifier correctly failed with 1/3 steps passing.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault failure (TN): the verifier correctly scored binary_reward 0 with only step 76.1 passing and fractional reward 0.333 because compute_kld failed its assertion and scan_sequence returned None where an integer position was expected [1]. The task required KLD and window log-odds against a uniform 0.25 background, PWM motif insertion into a uniformly drawn sequence, and repeated sliding-window scanning against scale·KLD [2][6], but the agent implemented compute_kld and scan_sequence with np.log2 rather than natural logarithms [3], whereas the reference uses np.log throughout [4], yielding a KLD of roughly 14.59 instead of the expected 10.11 on the canonical PWM fixture. The agent's generate_dna kept the background at length N and overwrote a motif window with p drawn from randint(0, N-L) [3], instead of splicing a PWM-sampled motif into a uniform length-N draw at p in [0, N-1] and building the reverse complement from that splice as the reference does [5], so chained step-76.4 tests that call generate_dna then scan_sequence could not recover the HDF5 target binding positions [6][1]. After an initial failed heredoc shell write, the agent saved solution.py via write_file and declared the implementation complete without executing any self-tests [7], even though its own reasoning noted ambiguity about log bases and insertion semantics. The task was not genuinely accomplished and the verifier's FAIL is fair.
